result.response:
The requirement specified that ambiguous local times during a Daylight Saving Time (DST) cutover overlap must resolve to the earlier instant across all time zones, including zones with a standard offset of zero (such as `Europe/London`).

### Root Cause
In [`DateTimeZone.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_19_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/DateTimeZone.java#L900), the method `getOffsetFromLocal` checked `else if (offsetLocal > 0)` to inspect previous transitions during potential DST overlaps. For time zones with a standard offset of `00:00` (e.g. `Europe/London`), `offsetLocal` during standard time is `0`. Because `0 > 0` evaluates to `false`, the DST overlap check was bypassed, causing local times during the autumn cutover to incorrectly resolve to the later instant (GMT) rather than the earlier daylight saving instant (BST).

### Fix
Changed the condition in [`DateTimeZone.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_19_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/DateTimeZone.java#L900) from `else if (offsetLocal > 0)` to `else if (offsetLocal >= 0)`.

### Verification
* Ran `TestDateTimeZoneCutover`, which contains `testDateTimeCreation_london`: all 116 tests in the suite passed.
* Saved the patch containing only source modifications to [`nl_fix.patch`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_19_group_b_fix/nl_fix.patch).
